text:
ash: seeing a spike of Pending GPU pods in us-west-2-small-gpu nodepool, looks like binpack failure / no-fit even though cluster has free GPUs across other pools

maria: are these fractional GPU requests or full gpu requests?

ash: full GPUs (nvidia-t4), but requests=1 limits=1, nodepool autoscaler isn't creating new nodes because of taints + kube-scheduler fit. pods show `0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match pod's nodeSelector.`

kevin: hmm that sounds like nodeSelector / nodeAffinity mismatch. Any recent changes to taints/labels on the small-gpu pool?

ash: we did add a `gpu-tier=small` label to avoid mixing with large-gpu jobs last week. some jobs have `gpu-type: any` but cores/memory requests differ. this is causing spread across pools and prevents tight binpack.

jae: can you paste the pod describe/events?

ash: ```
Name:           model-train-xyz-0
Status:         Pending
Conditions:     Initialized
                Ready            False   0s
Events:
  Type     Reason            Age   From               Message
  ----     ------            ----  ----               -------
  Normal   Scheduled         2m    default-scheduler  0/4 nodes are available: 2 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate, 2 node(s) didn't match node selector.
```

maria: that event line is key. autoscaler won't scale if pods are unschedulable due to nodeSelector mismatch. autoscaler only considers capacity/gpu availability, not label mismatches.

kevin: short-term fix: remove `gpu-tier` label on small pool so scheduler can pack pods into any pool with compatible GPU; longer-term we need instance-type-aware scheduling rules.

ash: removing label might increase cross-pool mixing which we wanted to avoid for cost reasons (small GPUs on cheaper spot instances). worried about spot evictions.

jae: alternative: add `nodeAffinity` to pods to prefer small-gpu but tolerate large-gpu, e.g., `preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution` so they can fall back to another pool when small pool is full.

maria: also consider enabling `autoscaler --scale-down-delay` tweaks? Not helpful here if pods are unschedulable due to labels.

kevin: for cost: we could set a binpack controller that packs by GPU model and memory, and then autoscaler can scale mixed node types. But that's more infra work.

ash: another wrinkle: we're seeing some pods stuck because the CNI returns "no route to host" during init on new nodes. suspect race between node registration and node-provisioning security groups. ops noticed network setup scripts run asynchronously on spot nodes.

jae: cc @sre-bot can we get a rolling check that new GPU nodes have the CNI and security groups applied before marking Ready? maybe an init taint until bootstrap complete.

sre-bot: noted. I'll open an infra ticket to add a bootstrap-check on node ready. adding a short `node.kubernetes.io/bootstrap-pending:No` taint removal step. (ticket INF-8421)

maria: for immediate relief I suggest: 1) relax nodeSelector on the training job to allow fallback 2) add preferredAffinity for `gpu-tier=small` 3) temporarily widen autoscaler quotas on us-west-2-small-gpu pool so it can scale up faster.

ash: will try 1+2 now, and file a request for pool quota bump. posting patch in #eng-infra after changes. :thumbsup:

kevin: once stable we should add an automated test that simulates label mismatches + autoscaler behavior. saved us time on similar incident last month.

ash: thanks all — I'll update thread after the patch.

(reacted with :eyes: by maria, kevin)
